prompt: Walk a sealed Expr tree of records with instanceof pattern matching: write eval and show for Num, Add, Mul and Neg. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A sealed interface lists its permitted implementations, so a chain of instanceof tests over those four records is genuinely exhaustive -- nothing else can ever implement Expr. Pattern matching for instanceof (Java 16) binds the tested value to an already-cast variable, so "e instanceof Add a" replaces a test, a cast and a local declaration with one line. Both methods are recursive because the shape of the data is recursive: each branch asks the same method about its children and combines the answers.
hints: Handle the null case and the Num leaf first -- those are the two places the recursion stops.
Records give you accessor methods named after the components, so an Add called a exposes a.left() and a.right().
Each branch calls eval or show on its children, so "(" + show(a.left()) + " + " + show(a.right()) + ")" builds the text for Add.
